paragraphs: MedLex Solutions is the first specialised forensic psychiatry training and consultation centre in the MENA region. We work along two lines that reinforce each other: structured training that equips psychiatrists with the forensic competence courts expect, and expert consultation that gives judicial and governmental institutions evaluations they can rely on.

The method is deliberately unglamorous — defined questions, documented reasoning, traceable sources, and conclusions stated at the confidence the evidence actually supports. That structure is what makes an opinion admissible, and it is also what protects the clinician who signed it.

We are not importing a model wholesale. Programmes are built around the legal frameworks practitioners here actually appear under, then aligned with international forensic standards rather than the other way round.

profile.name: Dr. Ahmed Abouelghit
profile.caption: DR. AHMED ABOUELGHIT · CONSULTANT
paragraphs: Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist, UK-trained, with broad international experience across Egypt, the United Kingdom, and Qatar. His work sits at the intersection of psychiatry, law, and institutional practice, with a focus on forensic assessment, medico-legal opinion, and the standards required in legally sensitive clinical settings.

As Forensic Psychiatry Training Program Director, he is actively involved in advancing specialist education and promoting high standards in forensic practice. His medico-legal experience was shaped in the United Kingdom across mental health tribunals, Magistrates' Courts, Crown Court, and the Parole Board - a practical understanding of how psychiatric opinion is examined in legal settings.

Alongside senior clinical and educational roles, he has contributed to professional training across the region, including consultancy work with UNICEF in Egypt supporting legal authorities. Through MedLex, he offers expert-led, court-conscious, and practice-grounded guidance in forensic and medico-legal psychiatry.

casc-academy.title: The CASC, from the examiner’s chair.
casc-academy.intro: An interactive, self-paced preparation platform for the MRCPsych CASC — designed and written by a former Royal College of Psychiatrists CASC examiner.

audience.title: What the CASC really tests
audience.body: The CASC is a station-based exam: a series of timed clinical encounters, observed and marked in real time.

items.title: Knowledge under pressure
items.body: The CASC does not test what you know on paper. It tests what you say, what you do, and what you decide — observed, against the clock, in a consultation style that examiners recognise instantly.

items.title: A designed assessment
items.body: Candidates rarely fail the CASC because they know too little psychiatry. They fail because they have never practised making the right moves, in the right order, in the way the station is designed to reward.

feature.title: Preparation today comes in two forms. Both are useful. Neither is enough.
feature.body: Recorded video courses explain concepts. Face-to-face teaching provides feedback. The missing layer is deliberate, examiner-guided practice: structured, repeatable rehearsal of the decisions each station is built to assess.
feature.quote: Available whenever you study, for as long as you need it — with feedback framed the way an examiner actually marks.

sampleStation.title: A station, in miniature
sampleStation.subtitle: A shortened taster of how Academy stations work. Full stations unfold over several decision points - this one gives you a single moment, and the examiner's view of it
sampleStation.meta: SAMPLE STATION - SPEAKING WITH A RELATIVE - COMMUNICATION & CONFIDENTIALITY
sampleStation.scenario: Daniel, 24, has been admitted with a first episode of psychosis. He has told the team clearly that he does not want clinical information shared with his family. His mother, distressed, has asked to speak with you. Speak with her.
sampleStation.question: She asks you directly: "Just tell me - is it schizophrenia?" What do you do first?

options.text: Reassure her by sharing the likely diagnosis - she is his mother, and she clearly cares about him
options.examinerFeedback: The instinct to comfort is human - and it is exactly where marks leak in this station. Daniel has explicitly declined to share, and disclosing the likely diagnosis breaches that. Strong candidates hold the boundary without abandoning warmth; this option abandons the boundary to keep the warmth.

options.text: Explain warmly that you cannot share Daniel's clinical information without his agreement - then explore her concerns, and offer what you can: general information, support for her, and a way forward
options.examinerFeedback: This is what the station is built to reward: the boundary is held, and the relationship is kept. You have declined to disclose, stayed with her distress, and opened a path forward - general information, support, and the possibility of Daniel choosing to involve her. The station rewards doing both at once, not choosing between them.

options.text: Tell her that confidentiality rules prevent you discussing anything, and suggest she raises her questions with Daniel himself
options.examinerFeedback: Technically defensible - and it stalls in the communication domain. The task was to manage this conversation, not to end it. Citing the rule and stepping back reads as dismissive, and the marks for engaging with her distress go uncollected.

sampleStation.testingTitle: WHAT THIS STATION IS REALLY TESTING
sampleStation.testingBody: Not your knowledge of confidentiality - every candidate knows the rule. It is testing whether you can hold a boundary and a relationship at the same time, under time pressure.
sampleStation.disclaimer: This sample uses an original teaching scenario built on the examination's publicly defined competency domains. Select the other options to compare the examiner's view of each.

faqs.question: Does the Academy replace a live course or my study group?
faqs.answer: No — and it does not try to. It gives the structured practice layer that most preparation is missing, so your live teaching and study partners are more useful.

faqs.question: Does it reveal real examination content?
faqs.answer: No. The Academy is built entirely on publicly defined competency domains and original scenarios, not recalled examination material.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for international medical graduates?
faqs.answer: It was designed with international candidates foremost in mind. All material is written in clear English and reflects the consultation style the examination expects.

faqs.question: When does it launch, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: Launch and pricing are announced to the waitlist first. Registering your interest carries no commitment.
